skill.name: datacommons-client
skill.description: Work with Data Commons public statistical data through the Python client. Use it to resolve places, query observations, explore graph relationships, and prepare results for analysis.
skill.summary: Query public statistics and entity metadata from Data Commons.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: The static alerts are false positives from Markdown examples, Data Commons client method names, and placeholder API key guidance. No evidence found of prompt injection, hidden network callbacks, credential exfiltration, command injection, or malicious intent. The main operational concerns are transparent network use, API key hygiene, and optional dependency installation.

remediation.issue: API key examples include an inline placeholder form.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer environment variables or secret managers, and warn users not to commit real keys.

remediation.issue: Installation examples may cause package installation in the user environment.
remediation.suggestion: State that users should install the Data Commons client only in trusted project environments.

remediation.issue: The skill makes external Data Commons API calls by design.
remediation.suggestion: Document that queries, place names, coordinates, and selected variables may be sent to Data Commons or a configured endpoint.

content.value_statement: Public statistics often require resolving entities, variables, and source metadata before analysis. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through Data Commons queries and result preparation.
actual_capabilities: Resolve place names, coordinates, and Wikidata IDs to Data Commons IDs.
Query observations for population, economy, health, and environment variables.
Fetch time series data and latest statistical values for entities.
Explore graph properties, place hierarchies, and entity names.
Convert observation responses into records for Pandas analysis.
Filter observations by source facets for consistent provenance.
limitations: Requires Data Commons API access and may need a user API key.
Resolve examples focus on place entities, not every graph entity type.
Data availability depends on Data Commons sources and update schedules.
The skill provides guidance, not independent data validation or forecasting.

use_cases.title: Compare Regional Indicators
use_cases.description: Resolve states, counties, or cities and compare population, income, and unemployment variables.

use_cases.title: Prepare Research Datasets
use_cases.description: Find reliable public data, retrieve time series, and shape results for notebooks or reports.

use_cases.title: Explore Place Metadata
use_cases.description: Navigate place hierarchies, inspect graph properties, and identify related entities before querying statistics.

prompt_templates.title: Find a Basic Statistic
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner query for one public statistic.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Data Commons to find the latest population for California. Explain the entity ID, variable, and source context.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Places
prompt_templates.prompt: Resolve California, Texas, and Florida, then compare latest population and unemployment rate values in a concise table.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Time Series
prompt_templates.prompt: Retrieve all available United States unemployment rate observations, prepare them for Pandas, and note any source consistency concerns.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Hierarchy Query
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow using graph relationships and source filters.
prompt_templates.prompt: Find all counties in California, query median household income for 2020, filter to a consistent source, and summarize outliers.

output_examples.input: Compare latest population for California, Texas, and New York.
output: A resolved entity list with Data Commons IDs for each state.
A comparison table showing the latest available population values.
A short note about the observation date and data source facets.

output_examples.input: Find time series data for United States unemployment.
output: A clean time series summary ordered by date.
Guidance for converting the response into a Pandas record table.
A provenance note recommending facet filtering when sources differ.

output_examples.input: Resolve San Francisco coordinates and query local indicators.
output: The matching place identifier and readable place name.
A selected list of available statistical variables.
A suggested query plan for population and income indicators.

best_practices: Resolve names to Data Commons IDs before querying observations.
Check available variables before requesting large datasets.
Use facet filters when results must come from one source family.
anti_patterns: Do not hardcode real API keys in notebooks or source files.
Do not assume ambiguous place names map to the intended entity.
Do not compare mixed-source results without checking provenance facets.

faq.question: Does this skill require a Data Commons API key?
faq.answer: The default Data Commons service may require an API key. Store it in an environment variable or secret manager.

faq.question: Can it work with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill content is compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: What kinds of data can I query?
faq.answer: You can query public demographic, economic, health, environmental, and other statistical variables available in Data Commons.

faq.question: Can it resolve city or state names automatically?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains name, coordinate, and Wikidata resolution for place entities.

faq.question: Does the skill validate the accuracy of Data Commons data?
faq.answer: No. It helps retrieve and inspect data. Users should review sources, facets, and methodology.

faq.question: Can results be used with Pandas?
faq.answer: Yes. The references show how to convert observation responses into record tables for Pandas analysis.
